report:
## Conclusion: Your skepticism is well supported by the evidence

The claim that increasing the number of childhood vaccines causes autism is not supported by rigorous science, and the large body of high-quality research contradicts it.

**Direct evidence on vaccine "load" and autism:** The key study addressing this specific claim is DeStefano et al. (2013), a CDC case-control study of ~1,000 children that found no association between the number of vaccine antigens received in the first two years of life and autism risk (https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2013/03/29/175626824/the-number-of-early-childhood-vaccines-not-linked-to-autism). Broader reviews of the totality of evidence, including a 2021/2022 synthesis, conclude that no plausible biological mechanism has been found linking vaccine quantity, timing, or ingredients to autism, despite extensive scrutiny (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8694782/).

**MMR-specific evidence:** The largest cohort study, Hviid et al. (2019, Denmark, 657,461 children), found no increased autism risk from MMR vaccination, including in high-risk subgroups, and no clustering of cases after vaccination (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30831578/). This built on earlier large Danish/international cohorts reaching the same conclusion.

**Counterpoint worth noting:** In November 2025, the CDC controversially revised its website to say the claim "vaccines do not cause autism" is "not evidence-based," reversing decades of agency position under new leadership. However, independent fact-checkers found this change misrepresented the underlying research and was widely condemned by scientists and autism researchers as not reflecting the actual evidence base (https://www.factcheck.org/2025/11/revised-cdc-website-about-autism-and-vaccines-is-not-evidence-based/).

**Bottom line:** Multiple large, independent, methodologically strong studies find no link between vaccine quantity/schedule and autism; the 2025 CDC reversal is a political/administrative outlier, not a reflection of new contrary scientific findings.
